extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers, magazine readers, librarians, and book reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Implicit evaluative criteria and production requirements drawn from Victorian magazine book reviews and the attached Project Gutenberg distribution license; covers how to judge/prepare biographical and pedagogical editions, accessibility, and legal/redistribution obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity and focus in short biographies
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographies should be short and well written, graphic and picturesque without being in the least diffuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketches can range from five to fifteen pages; avoid unnecessary diffusion, but omit no essential fact in the career or essential trait in the character of those treated. Make concrete facts bring history nearer to the imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of subjects for a biographical compendium
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the great leading personages in the arts of peace who exemplified human progress among the English-speaking races, and arrange them in chronological order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose figures likely to interest young readers (boys especially), and include emblematically embellished portraits to enhance appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced moral judgment in biographies
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not pass lightly over the errors of a subject but recognize peculiar position and circumstances; balance condemnation with palliation where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present context that explains apparent paradoxes (e.g., public errors vs. private virtues), allowing readers to see how a person may be 'as noble and upright as the saint' despite social deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial tone: discriminating and sympathetic touch
rubrics_metrics.description: The biographer/critic should use a nice and discriminating touch—acknowledging faults without losing sight of the subject's virtues and achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid moralistic doctrinaire judgments; aim for sympathetic, nuanced treatment rather than harsh condemnation or uncritical praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation of classic works for local students
rubrics_metrics.description: When editing or abridging a classic (e.g., Mill's Principles), add results of later thinking that do not contradict the original views and adapt illustrations to fit the facts peculiar to the local (American) students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abridge without impairing lucidity; avoid technicality and abstractness; mark editorial additions typographically (e.g., smaller type) so readers can distinguish original text from notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving lucidity and accessibility in abridgements
rubrics_metrics.description: A compact arrangement should retain the original author's lucidity while reducing bulk to attract readers frightened by larger editions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep explanations clear and readable; prioritize accessibility over exhaustive technical detail for use as a college text-book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of exegetical commentary depends on audience and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Exegetical commentaries on sacred texts are useful insofar as they provide genuine exegetical illumination and either originality or faithful orthodoxy suited to their intended audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sound orthodox comments may serve 'poor pious souls' in rural areas, but lack of freshness and originality reduces broader value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for adapting scholarly histories for children
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplification and condensation for young readers must be done with taste and good judgment to retain interest and essential stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell specially interesting stories neatly, arrange them in chronological order, use sufficiently simple language, include handsome illustrations, and ensure good typography and binding for a holiday or children's edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness without verbosity in short sketches
rubrics_metrics.description: Short sketches should be complete in essentials—omitting no essential fact or essential trait—while avoiding diffusive detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for narrative compactness: give the full account appropriate to the sketch length (5–15 pages) but do not overload with minutiae that obscure the main life arc or character traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrative portraits and typographic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Include portraits and maintain high typographic and binding standards to increase the attractiveness and utility of a book, especially for younger readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emblematically embellished portraits and handsome printing/binding make condensed or juvenile editions more creditable and appealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategical assessment criteria for geographic/military value
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate an island's (Heligoland) strategical value by its situation relative to river mouths, command of sea approaches, proximity to trade centres, and suitability for fortification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also weigh cost of purchase/fortification, diplomatic consequences (how other powers will construe transfer), alternative means to achieve defensive objectives, and the wider probability of hostilities between the concerned powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial honesty in indicating added material
rubrics_metrics.description: Make editorial notes and additions clearly distinguishable from the original text (e.g., printed in smaller type), so readers can separate original authorial content from later commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aids pedagogical use and preserves the integrity of the original work while providing helpful modernizing notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg: keep full license with redistributed works
rubrics_metrics.description: When redistributing a Project Gutenberg electronic work, the full Project Gutenberg License must remain attached and the required license sentence must appear prominently with active links or immediate access to the full license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not unlink, detach, or remove the full Project Gutenberg License terms from the work; prominently display the specified sentence whenever any copy is accessed, displayed, performed, viewed, copied, or distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg trademark and attribution rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Project Gutenberg' trademark may only be used on or associated with an electronic work by people who agree to be bound by the full license; if you remove Project Gutenberg references you may copy the underlying public-domain text but must not use the trademark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To preserve the Project Gutenberg name associated with the work, the Foundation asks redistributors to keep the work in the same format with its attached full license; special trademark license terms apply for commercial use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg: requirements for alternate formats
rubrics_metrics.description: If you provide the work in a format other than the official 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' (or other official posted format), you must, at no additional cost, provide a copy or means to obtain the original plain form upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any alternate format must include the full Project Gutenberg License as specified; conversions to binary, compressed, marked up, or proprietary forms are permitted only if the original form remains available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg: charging fees and royalty obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not charge a fee for access to or distribution of Project Gutenberg works unless you comply with the license's commercial terms; charging is permitted only if you pay a royalty of 20% of gross profits (with reporting and timing requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The royalty is owed to the owner of the Project Gutenberg trademark and must be paid within 60 days following tax-reporting periods; additional requirements in the license must also be followed for commercial redistribution.
